reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: I reviewed the resource-review contract, resource assessment rubric, fresh-review framework, supplied Condition context, deterministic aggregate, full Condition structure report, and the R4/R6 Condition StructureDefinitions for the status, evidence, stage, body-location, actor, and category deltas. I also checked the behavior reports for findings whose affectedResources include Condition; none were direct Condition behavior findings. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context, consistent with the contract.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 Condition is a mature trial-use clinical resource. FMM 3 does not freeze the model, but it creates meaningful pressure to avoid avoidable hard instance breaks, especially where status semantics can affect clinical interpretation, decision support, quality reporting, or problem-list workflows.

overall.oneLineConclusion: Condition keeps its identity but has targeted hard breaks around status, entered-in-error handling, evidence, and stage assessment, so migration work is likely while low-cost compatibility preservation still matters.

reasoning.thesisMd: Condition is not removed or replaced, and most of the resource remains recognizable across R4 and R6. The resource-level migration burden is nevertheless real because R6 requires `clinicalStatus`, removes the R4 entered-in-error exception, rewrites `Condition.evidence` from an R4 backbone to `CodeableReference`, and narrows `stage.assessment` by dropping `ClinicalImpression`. That combination justifies planning a targeted Condition migration program, but it does not make every additional break irrelevant.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The actual migration shape is a moderate targeted remodel. Status governance is the central workstream: R4 instances with omitted `clinicalStatus` need policy-driven values, and entered-in-error records need special handling because R4 forbade the field while R6 requires it. Evidence requires a structural transform from grouped `code`/`detail` backbone entries to R6 `CodeableReference` entries, with possible loss of grouping semantics. Stage assessment references to `ClinicalImpression` require remediation. The remaining findings are mostly additive, widening, weakening, or reverse-direction issues rather than R4-to-R6 hard breaks.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: A migration program is already plausible for serious Condition implementers, but compatibility leverage remains meaningful. For changes tied to a coherent R6 design goal, such as a universal modifier-status guarantee or reuse of `CodeableReference`, local migration may be the right cost. For changes that could be preserved with modest base-model cost, especially the entered-in-error status exception and the `ClinicalImpression` target, preventing the break still has high value even though other Condition migration work exists.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest less-breaking alternatives are narrow: keep `clinicalStatus` optional only when `verificationStatus` is entered-in-error, and retain `ClinicalImpression` as an allowed `stage.assessment` target while discouraging or profiling it where needed. Keeping `clinicalStatus` optional for all Conditions would preserve more R4 data but would weaken the R6 modifier-status guarantee. Keeping both the old evidence backbone and new `CodeableReference` shape would create duplicate representations and precedence questions, so that break is more plausibly a local migration chore once the R6 remodel is accepted.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior finding applied to Condition. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings are relevant to generic FHIR clients and server conformance, but they are not Condition-specific resource migration drivers under the supplied contract.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate's `Partial` major-migration conclusion, `moderate-targeted-remodel` shape, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration` posture match my independent judgment. The important nuance is that `Partial` should not be read as a reason to discount the two avoidable local breaks; it means the unavoidable work is targeted rather than a whole-resource replacement.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the structural deltas because the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions were available locally. The main uncertainty is terminology detail for the R6 clinical-status value set because the local package does not include the full external CodeSystem expansion, and implementation prevalence of `evidence` grouping or `ClinicalImpression` stage references is not measured here.

findingConsiderations.title: Condition.clinicalStatus is now mandatory
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a common, high-impact old-valid/new-invalid break: R4 allowed many Conditions to omit `clinicalStatus`, while R6 requires it. It drives the need for a status-audit migration workstream. I do not treat it as clearly avoidable at resource level because R6 has a credible safety/computability rationale for requiring an explicit modifier status or `unknown`.

findingConsiderations.title: Entered-in-error Conditions changed from forbidding clinicalStatus to requiring it
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the strongest avoidable compatibility concern. R4's entered-in-error pattern and R6's mandatory status are directly incompatible, and a low-cost less-breaking design appears available: keep the R4 exception or require status conditionally only outside entered-in-error. This matters even if general status migration is accepted.

findingConsiderations.title: Condition.evidence changed from a BackboneElement with code/detail to CodeableReference
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The evidence rewrite is a non-mechanical hard break for wire format, generated models, FHIRPath, and grouping semantics. It materially contributes to the targeted migration program, but a parallel legacy backbone would create duplicate same-resource evidence representations, so this looks more like an accepted remodel chore than a low-cost preservation candidate.

findingConsiderations.title: Condition.stage.assessment no longer allows ClinicalImpression references
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Dropping `ClinicalImpression` creates a hard break for existing references while retaining the target in base R6 would be a narrow, low-cost compatibility mechanism. Unless there is a strong safety or semantic rationale for excluding it, this should remain standards-review-worthy rather than being dismissed as part of the broader Condition migration.

findingConsiderations.title: Condition.clinicalStatus required binding now documents an `unknown` status
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Adding `unknown` is not an R4-to-R6 hard break and is arguably necessary once `clinicalStatus` is mandatory. It still matters for downgrade and enum-based clients, so migration guidance should explicitly handle how R6 `unknown` maps, or fails to map, back to R4.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds native Condition.bodyStructure and forbids using it with bodySite
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is not a base R4-to-R6 hard break because `bodySite` remains and the new element is optional. It is still a local mapping chore for systems that used the R4 body-structure extension or need R6-to-R4 downgrade, but it does not drive the resource-level break-avoidance conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: Condition.recorder and Condition.asserter allow additional R6 reference targets
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This widens R4-to-R6 validation and mainly creates R6-to-R4 representability and client-assumption risks for Group or Device actors. It is a profile/client update issue, not a reason to classify Condition as broadly remodeled.

findingConsiderations.title: Condition.category binding weakened from extensible to example
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Weakening a binding is not an old-valid/new-invalid break. Implementations that depend on R4's stronger category guidance should restate it in R6 profiles, but this is semantic/conformance drift rather than a migration blocker.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This and related Resource-level operation removals can affect generic FHIR clients used with Condition, but the finding is assigned to shared `Resource` behavior rather than to Condition. It should be handled in the shared behavior review, not counted as a Condition resource-model break.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is shared Resource/DomainResource search metadata context. It may affect generic search tooling, but it is not a direct Condition search surface change and does not alter the Condition-specific migration shape.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit the entered-in-error/status interaction in the base Condition design. A conditional exception preserving the R4 entered-in-error pattern appears to reduce incompatibility without undermining ordinary Condition status requirements.

Ask the Patient Care work group to confirm the rationale for removing `ClinicalImpression` from `Condition.stage.assessment`; if there is no strong reason, retain it as a deprecated or discouraged base target.

Publish explicit migration guidance and test cases for missing `clinicalStatus`, R4 entered-in-error records, and `Condition.evidence` conversion to and from `CodeableReference`, including grouping-loss warnings.
Document local downgrade/profile choices for R6-only concerns: `clinicalStatus=unknown`, native `bodyStructure`, Group/Device actor references, and the weaker `category` binding.

caveats: The local R6 package did not include the full external `condition-clinical` CodeSystem expansion, so exact terminology-code comparison has medium uncertainty.
No direct behavior finding listed Condition as an affected resource; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior was intentionally kept context-only.
Prevalence of omitted status, evidence usage, and ClinicalImpression stage references is implementation-dependent; this review judges base compatibility risk, not measured deployment frequency.
